        "statement": "Let $D\\subseteq\\mathbb R^2$ be a compact finite elementary Green region with its positive boundary orientation and let $I\\subseteq\\mathbb R$ be an interval. Let $r:D\\times I\\to\\mathbb R^3$ extend to a $C^2$ map on a neighbourhood of $D\\times I$ with $r_u\\times r_v\\ne0$ on the interior, and require the images to be embedded if an actual material sheet is intended. Define the velocity $v$ on a neighbourhood of the swept surface by $v(r(u,v,t),t):=\\partial_tr(u,v,t)$, requiring it to be single-valued and of class $C^1$. For a $C^1$ field $B$ on a neighbourhood of the swept set, the flux through the patch at time $t$ is $$\\Phi(t):=\\int_D\\bigl\\langle B(r(u,v,t),t),\\,r_u(u,v,t)\\times r_v(u,v,t)\\bigr\\rangle\\,du\\,dv.$$",

        "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$). Let $\\Omega\\subseteq\\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $S\\subset\\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\\Omega_-$ to the side $\\Omega_+$, and put $\\delta_S(\\psi):=\\int_S\\psi\\,dS$ for $\\psi\\in\\mathcal D(\\Omega)$, the surface integral being that of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]].         "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$). Let $a>0$ and let $\\rho\\in L^1(\\mathbb R^3)$ vanish outside $\\{y:\\lvert y\\rvert\\le a\\}$. Put $Q:=\\int\\rho$, $p:=\\int y\\,\\rho(y)\\,dy$ and $\\lVert\\rho\\rVert_1:=\\int\\lvert\\rho\\rvert$. Then for every $x$ with $r:=\\lvert x\\rvert\\ge2a>0$, $$\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\frac{\\rho(y)}{\\lvert x-y\\rvert}\\,dy=\\frac Qr+\\frac{p\\cdot x}{r^3}+R(x),\\qquad \\lvert R(x)\\rvert\\le\\frac{16\\,a^2\\lVert\\rho\\rVert_1}{r^3}.$$",
        "strategy": "Set $h(s)=\\lvert x-sy\\rvert^{-1}$; $h$ is $C^2$ on $[0,1]$ and the identity $h(1)-h(0)-h'(0)=\\int_0^1(1-s)h''(s)\\,ds$ follows from the fundamental theorem applied to $\\frac{d}{ds}[(1-s)h'(s)+h(s)]=(1-s)h''(s)$. Because $\\lvert x-sy\\rvert\\ge r-a\\ge r/2$ for $r\\ge2a$, one has $\\lvert h''(s)\\rvert\\le4\\lvert y\\rvert^2/(r-a)^3\\le32\\lvert y\\rvert^2/r^3$, and integrating against $\\lvert\\rho\\rvert$ gives the bound with $C=16$, which is permissible but not sharp.         "statement": "Let $K\\subseteq\\mathbb R^n$ be compact, measurable and of finite Lebesgue measure, let $a<b$, and let $f$ and $\\partial_tf$ be continuous on a neighbourhood of $K\\times[a,b]$.         "statement": "Let (V,eta) be the Lorentz vector space and let (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an ordered eta-orthonormal basis with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1).         "statement": "Adopt the postulates of the spacetime-primitives page: the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) as the spacetime of the framework with the equations of the specified model covariant under proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps, which are the inertial changes of description (post-sr-inertial-covariance), and the ideal clock and ideal light assumptions, including that ideal vacuum light rays are the future null straight lines and that inertial charts use x^0 = c t (post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light, def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions).         "inventory_expansion_required": false,
        "statement": "Let $n\\ge1$, let $U\\subseteq\\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $\\theta_0\\in U$, and let $u\\in\\mathbb R^n$ satisfy $\\lVert u\\rVert_2=1$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Let $I\\subseteq\\mathbb R$ be an open interval with $0\\in I$ and such that $\\gamma(\\theta):=\\theta_0+\\theta u\\in U$ for every $\\theta\\in I$. Let $F:U\\to\\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $F(\\theta_0)=0$, and suppose that for every $\\theta\\in I$ the directional derivative of $F$ along $u$ satisfies\n$$D_uF(\\theta_0+\\theta u)=\\langle\\nabla F(\\theta_0+\\theta u),u\\rangle\\ge m>0$$\n([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], [[thm-gradient-represents-directional-derivatives-and-steepest-ascent]]). Let a recorded scalar $\\hat y\\in\\mathbb R$ satisfy $|\\hat y|\\le s$ with $s\\ge0$, and let a calibration-error bound $|y-\\hat y|\\le\\delta$ with $\\delta\\ge0$ hold for $y:=F(\\theta_0+\\theta u)$ at a candidate $\\theta\\in I$. Then\n$$|\\theta|\\le\\frac{s+\\delta}{m},$$\nand the corresponding configuration displacement $\\gamma(\\theta)-\\theta_0=\\theta u$ has Euclidean length $\\lVert\\theta u\\rVert_2=|\\theta|$. The conclusion is a deterministic conditional statement about the stated bounds; it is not a sampling law, a statistical inference, or a claim about any historical report, and the parameters $s,\\delta,m$ are supplied by the user of the statement rather than estimated from data here.",
        "strategy": "Set $\\gamma(\\theta):=\\theta_0+\\theta u$ and $g:=F\\circ\\gamma:I\\to\\mathbb R$, and verify the hypotheses of the bounded-error model-comparison lemma for $g$ on $I$ before reading off its conclusion. (i) Each component $\\theta\\mapsto(\\theta_0)_j+\\theta u_j$ of $\\gamma$ is a sum of a constant and a scalar multiple of the identity $\\theta\\mapsto\\theta^1$, hence differentiable with derivative $u_j$ ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). These partial derivatives are the constant functions $u_j$, so they exist on the open interval $I$ and are continuous there; [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]] therefore makes $\\gamma$ totally differentiable at every $\\theta\\in I$ with $D\\gamma(\\theta)$ the linear map whose matrix is $J\\gamma(\\theta)$ ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), that is, $D\\gamma(\\theta)(h)=hu$ for $h\\in\\mathbb R$. (ii) Both $F$ (on the open set $U$) and $\\gamma$ (on the open interval $I$) are covered by the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]), so $g$ is totally differentiable at every $\\theta\\in I$ with $Dg(\\theta)=DF(\\gamma(\\theta))\\circ D\\gamma(\\theta)$. For a real-valued function on an open subset of $\\mathbb R$ the ordinary derivative is the total derivative applied to $1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), so $g'(\\theta)=DF(\\gamma(\\theta))(u)=D_uF(\\gamma(\\theta))=\\langle\\nabla F(\\gamma(\\theta)),u\\rangle\\ge m$ by the hypothesis ([[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-gradient-represents-directional-derivatives-and-steepest-ascent]]). (iii) The derivative $g'=\\sum_j(\\partial_jF\\circ\\gamma)\\,u_j$ is continuous on $I$: the partial derivatives $\\partial_jF$ are continuous on $U$ because $F$ is $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); $\\gamma$ is continuous because $d_2(\\gamma(\\theta),\\gamma(\\theta'))=\\lVert(\\theta-\\theta')u\\rVert_2=|\\theta-\\theta'|$ by the homogeneity of the Euclidean norm and $\\lVert u\\rVert_2=1$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]], [[def-metric-continuity]]); each composite $\\partial_jF\\circ\\gamma$ is then continuous because for open $V\\subseteq\\mathbb R$ its preimage is $\\gamma^{-1}[\\partial_jF^{-1}[V]]$, the preimage under $\\gamma$ of an open set ([[thm-metric-continuity-characterisations]]); and $g'$ is a finite sum of scalar multiples of these composite functions, hence continuous as a real function on $I$ ([[lem-real-and-metric-notions-agree]], [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]]). Thus $g$ is $C^1$ on $I$ in the lemma's sense, and $g(0)=F(\\theta_0)=0$. Finally $\\lVert\\theta u\\rVert_2=|\\theta|\\,\\lVert u\\rVert_2=|\\theta|$ by homogeneity of the Euclidean norm and $\\lVert u\\rVert_2=1$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).         "statement": "(i) Specialise [[thm-em-uncertainty-analysis]] to $n=1$, $U=\\mathbb R$, $\\theta_0=0$, $u=1$, $I=\\mathbb R$ and $F(\\theta)=m\\theta$ with $m>0$. Fix the recorded value $\\hat y=0$ (so $s=0$) and any $\\delta\\ge0$. A candidate $\\theta\\in\\mathbb R$ is compatible with the calibration bound exactly when $|F(\\theta)-\\hat y|=|m\\theta|\\le\\delta$, that is, exactly when $|\\theta|\\le\\delta/m$; this is precisely the theorem's bound $(s+\\delta)/m=\\delta/m$, and the bound is attained (equality) at $\\theta=\\pm\\delta/m$. Hence the constant $(s+\\delta)/m$ cannot be improved for this instance, and the special case $\\delta=0$ leaves $\\theta=0$ as the only compatible candidate. (ii) The positive lower bound on the response is not removable. Multiplying the inequality $|\\theta|\\le\\delta/m$ by $m>0$ gives $|m\\theta|\\le\\delta$ and conversely, using $|m\\theta|=m|\\theta|$ and the defining clauses of the absolute value ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]]); at $\\theta=\\pm\\delta/m$ one has $|m\\theta|=\\delta$, so equality holds in the bound while the candidate remains compatible; and for $\\delta=0$ the inequality $|m\\theta|\\le0$ forces $m\\theta=0$, hence $\\theta=0$. (ii) For $F\\equiv0$ the gradient vanishes ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), so $\\langle\\nabla F(\\theta),u\\rangle=0$ is not $\\ge m$ for any $m>0$ and the theorem's hypothesis is not met; nevertheless $y=F(\\theta)=0=\\hat y$ for every $\\theta$, so $|y-\\hat y|=0\\le\\delta$ and $|\\hat y|=0\\le s$ hold for every $\\theta\\in\\mathbb R$: the data cannot confine the parameter at all.         "domain": "mathematics",
        "title": "Curves, regular causal curves and future timelike worldlines in affine Minkowski space",
        "statement": "Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) and let I be an order-convex subset of R with at least two elements (def-interval); a curve of the model is a map x: I -> A. (a) Derivative and regularity of the parametrization. For s in I and h nonzero with s + h in I the difference quotient (x(s+h) - x(s))/h is an element of V, the displacement from x(s) to x(s+h) divided by the real number h; the curve is differentiable at s when the limit of these quotients as h -> 0 exists in the finite-dimensional real vector space V, and then this limit, written x'(s) in V, is the tangent vector of x at s. If x_A: A -> R^4 is the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), then x is differentiable at s exactly when the R^4-valued map x_A o x is differentiable at s in the sense of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, and then x'(s) = E((x_A o x)'(s)), where E: R^4 -> V is the frame isomorphism; this does not depend on the inertial chart used, because inertial chart transitions are affine, hence smooth (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas), and all norms on the finite-dimensional V give the same limit. The curve is C^1 when it is differentiable at every point of I and the derivative map s |-> x'(s), I -> V, is continuous (def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity); it is C^k for k >= 1 when x' is C^{k-1}.         "statement": "Work in the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) with its inertial atlas (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas) and the canonical identification T_pA = V (lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v). The following objects are defined and are, in general, different objects. (a) Chart and inertial chart. A chart of the model is a diffeomorphism u: U -> u(U) from a nonempty open subset U of A onto an open subset of R^4 (def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds, def-smooth-manifold), written with components (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3). An inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) is the global chart x(p) = E^{-1}(p-o) of an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3). A general chart need not be inertial: if x is an inertial chart and N: x(U) -> R^4 is a diffeomorphism onto its image which is not the restriction of an affine map, then u := N o x is a chart that is not inertial, because if u were the inertial chart of a frame then x o u^{-1} = N^{-1} would be affine by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz and hence N = (N^{-1})^{-1} would be affine as the inverse of an affine bijection, a contradiction; the map N(y) = (y^0, y^1 + (y^0)^2, y^2, y^3) on R^4 is an explicit example. (b) Tetrad at an event and tetrad field. A tetrad at p in A is an ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of V with eta(e_a,e_b) = diag(-1,1,1,1)_{ab} and e_0 future (e_0 in C^+); this is an inertial frame's basis without an origin and without the orientation condition. A tetrad field on a nonempty open subset Omega of A is a tuple (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) of smooth vector fields on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, type (1,0)) whose values at every p form a tetrad at p; it is observer-adapted when E_0 = U/c for a prescribed future timelike worldline or congruence. (c) Observer congruence. An observer congruence on a nonempty open subset Omega of A is a smooth vector field n: Omega -> V with eta(n,n) = -1 and n(p) in C^+ for all p; its observers are its maximal integral curves (def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field, thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point), each of which is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); n is nowhere zero because it is unit. Completeness of the integral curves, a global product structure of Omega and global synchronization are not asserted. (d) Adapted chart. For a congruence n on Omega, an n-adapted chart is a chart (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3): U -> R^4 with U a nonempty open subset of Omega whose spatial coordinates u^1,u^2,u^3 are constant along every integral curve of n contained in U; no global adapted chart is asserted, and u^0 is not required to be affine. (e) Distinctions. A chart need not be inertial (a); a chart need not be n-adapted for any congruence; a tetrad field is not in general the coordinate frame of a chart: if (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) is the coordinate frame of a chart (v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3), i.e. E_a = partial/partial v^a, then [E_a,E_b] = 0 for all a,b (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields, prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket), so a tetrad field whose members do not commute pairwise is not a coordinate frame; no converse is claimed here. A congruence need not be a coordinate flow, and its pointwise rest spaces need not assemble into hypersurfaces; that integrability question is decided below on this page. In an inertial chart the coordinate frame is simultaneously an inertial frame's basis, a constant tetrad field and the congruence of stationary observers, but the four notions are distinct in general.",

        "id": "def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space",
        "kind": "definition",
        "domain": "mathematics",
        "title": "The flat covariant derivative on affine Minkowski space and fields along curves",
        "statement": "Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with tangent spaces canonically identified with V, and let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (a) Vector fields. For smooth vector fields X,Y on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space) define the covariant derivative of Y in the direction X at p by (nabla_X Y)(p) := (d/dt)|_{t=0} Y(p + t X(p)); in the inertial chart x of any inertial frame this is (nabla_X Y)^a = X^b partial_b Y^a. The value does not depend on the inertial chart: for another inertial chart x' = Lambda x + b one has partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b and Y'^a = Lambda^a_b Y^b (thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation), and Lambda is constant, so Lambda^a_c X'^b partial'_b Y'^c = X^b partial_b Y^a. nabla_X Y is again a smooth vector field. (b) Covector and general tensor fields. For a smooth covector field alpha set (nabla_X alpha)(Y) := X(alpha(Y)) - alpha(nabla_X Y); for a type (r,s) tensor field T define nabla_X T by the derivation rule on the evaluation of T on smooth vector and covector fields, subtracting nabla_X Y from each vector argument and adding it to each covector argument; in inertial coordinates every component of nabla_X T is X^b partial_b of the component, with no connection coefficients. (c) Properties. nabla is R-bilinear, C^infinity(Omega)-linear in X, satisfies nabla_X(fY) = X(f)Y + f nabla_X Y and the analogous Leibniz rules for tensor fields, is metric compatible (nabla eta = 0, because partial_a eta_{bc} = 0 in every inertial chart), is torsion-free (nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y], def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields and prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket) and has zero curvature (nabla_X nabla_Y Z - nabla_Y nabla_X Z - nabla_{[X,Y]} Z = 0), the last by equality of mixed partial derivatives of the components (thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem). (d) Fields along a curve. If gamma: I -> A is a C^1 curve and W: I -> V is a C^1 field along it (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve), the covariant derivative of W along gamma is the ordinary V-valued derivative DW/ds := W' (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral), because the canonical identification T_pA = V is independent of p; consequently parallel transport along any curve is the identity and a field is parallel exactly when it is constant. The derivative (d) is the one used for the acceleration of congruences, for Fermi-Walker transport and for the kinematic decomposition below; the model needs no Christoffel symbols or parallel-transport ODE in this formulation.",

(ii) The extension in (b) is the standard derivation rule on the evaluation of a tensor; the coordinate expression has no Gamma terms because eta is constant and transition matrices are constant in inertial charts.         "statement": "Let n be an observer congruence on a nonempty open subset Omega of A (def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction), let nabla be the flat covariant derivative (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space), and write n_b := eta_{bc} n^c for the associated covector field. Define h(v,w) := eta(v,w) + eta(n,v) eta(n,w) for vectors at the same point, so h = eta + n-flat (x) n-flat; then h(v,w) = eta(h(v),h(w)) where h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n is the orthogonal projection of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c). At every point h is symmetric with radical spanned by n(p), and its restriction to n(p)^perp is positive definite. (b) Acceleration. The acceleration of the congruence is a := nabla_n n; then eta(n,a) = 0 pointwise, because 2 eta(n, nabla_n n) = n(eta(n,n)) = 0, so a(p) is spacelike or zero by the causal classification. In the model's physical interpretation the four-acceleration of the congruence observers is c^2 a and its magnitude is c^2 sqrt(eta(a,a)); the numerical units belong to the model's SI conventions and are not part of the affine geometry. (c) Kinematic decomposition. Set theta_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{(c} n_{d)} and omega_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{[c} n_{d]}, where nabla_{(c} n_{d)} = (1/2)(nabla_c n_d + nabla_d n_c) and nabla_{[c} n_{d]} = (1/2)(nabla_c n_d - nabla_d n_c). (d) Born rigidity. The congruence is Born rigid (describes a rigid motion) if L_n h = 0.
